Rule used by the usb redirection filter to match USB devices and decide whether redirection is allowed. Each field is a matcher for the corresponding USB descriptor value; -1 in any field means “match any.” If a rule matches, allow==0 denies, nonzero allows. Rules are typically created via usbredirfilter_string_to_rules() and must be freed with usbredirfilter_free().

Opaque/partially exposed parser context for the usbredir protocol. Applications obtain it via usbredirparser_create, configure callbacks, then initialize with usbredirparser_init. It owns IO buffering and invokes user-provided callbacks for parsed packets. Do not allocate directly; lifetime is managed by create/destroy. Thread-lock callbacks can be supplied for multithreaded use.

functions.name: usbredirfilter_string_to_rules
functions.signature: int usbredirfilter_string_to_rules(const char *filter_str, const char *token_sep, const char *rule_sep, struct usbredirfilter_rule **rules_ret, int *rules_count_ret);
functions.description: Parses a textual USB redirection filter description into an array of usbredirfilter_rule structures. The filter string is tokenized using token_sep as the set of token separators and rule_sep as the set of rule separators (as with strtok). On success, allocates and returns a rules array and its count; the caller must free the returned array with usbredirfilter_free. Returns 0 on success, -ENOMEM if allocation fails, or -EINVAL on parsing error.
requirements: filter_str must point to a NUL-terminated string describing rules; format per rule: "<class>,<vendor>,<product>,<version>,<allow>" with token separators from token_sep and rules separated by characters from rule_sep.
token_sep must point to a NUL-terminated string specifying the set of token-separator characters (used like strtok).
rule_sep must point to a NUL-terminated string specifying the set of rule-separator characters (used like strtok).
rules_ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive an allocated array of struct usbredirfilter_rule; the caller must free it with usbredirfilter_free when done.
rules_count_ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the number of rules returned.

Each parsed rule field ranges (per struct usbredirfilter_rule): device_class 0–255 or -1; vendor_id 0–65535 or -1; product_id 0–65535 or -1; device_version_bcd 0–65535 or -1; allow: 0 denies, non-zero allows.
On error return (-ENOMEM or -EINVAL), no memory must be assumed to be returned via rules_ret; caller should not attempt to free unless a non-NULL value was stored.
Caller must check the integer return code and handle errors accordingly.

functions.name: usbredirfilter_rules_to_string
functions.signature: char *usbredirfilter_rules_to_string(const struct usbredirfilter_rule *rules, int rules_count, const char *token_sep, const char *rule_sep);
functions.description: Serializes a set of usbredirfilter_rule entries to a textual filter string suitable for usbredirfilter_string_to_rules. Returns an allocated C string on success; the caller must free it with usbredirfilter_free. Returns NULL if the rules fail verification or if memory allocation fails.
requirements: rules must point to an array of rules with length rules_count.
rules_count must be >= 0; for >0, rules must reference at least rules_count valid entries.
The rules are verified by the function; if any rule has out-of-bounds fields (see struct ranges), the function returns NULL.
token_sep must point to the set of token-separator characters to use when composing the string; rule_sep must point to the set of rule-separator characters.
Caller must check for NULL return and avoid using the result if NULL.
On success, the returned string must be freed with usbredirfilter_free.

functions.name: usbredirfilter_check
functions.signature: int usbredirfilter_check(const struct usbredirfilter_rule *rules, int rules_count, uint8_t device_class, uint8_t device_subclass, uint8_t device_protocol, uint8_t *interface_class, uint8_t *interface_subclass, uint8_t *interface_protocol, int interface_count, uint16_t vendor_id, uint16_t product_id, uint16_t device_version_bcd, int flags);
functions.description: Evaluates whether redirection of a USB device (identified by device- and interface-level class/subclass/protocol and by VID/PID/version) is allowed under the provided filter rules. The function performs multiple passes: first using the device class, then for each interface using the interface class info (with documented skips). Returns 0 if allowed, -EPERM if denied by a matching rule, -ENOENT if no rule matched during a pass (unless usbredirfilter_fl_default_allow is set), and -EINVAL for invalid parameters.
requirements: rules must point to an array of rules with length rules_count; the rules should satisfy the value ranges defined by struct usbredirfilter_rule or the function may return -EINVAL.
rules_count must be >= 0.
device_class/device_subclass/device_protocol are the device-level class descriptors as bytes (0–255).

interface_class/interface_subclass/interface_protocol must each point to arrays of length at least interface_count when interface_count > 0; they provide per-interface class/subclass/protocol bytes (0–255).
interface_count must be >= 0; if 0, no interface passes are performed.
vendor_id, product_id, device_version_bcd are 16-bit values (0–65535) describing the device.
flags is a combination of usbredirfilter_fl_default_allow (0x01) and/or usbredirfilter_fl_dont_skip_non_boot_hid (0x02).

Behavioral notes affecting results (not caller constraints): if device class is 0x00 or 0xef, the device-class pass is skipped; if usbredirfilter_fl_dont_skip_non_boot_hid is not set and the device has >1 interface with an interface of class 0x03, subclass 0x00, protocol 0x00, that interface’s pass is skipped; when no rule matches in a pass, result is -ENOENT unless usbredirfilter_fl_default_allow is set, in which case that pass allows.
Caller must check and handle the integer return code: 0 allow, -EINVAL invalid parameters, -EPERM blocked, -ENOENT no rule matched in a pass.

functions.name: usbredirfilter_verify
functions.signature: int usbredirfilter_verify(const struct usbredirfilter_rule *rules, int rules_count);
functions.description: Performs a sanity check on a rules array, ensuring field values are within documented bounds. Returns 0 on success or -EINVAL if any values are out of bounds.
requirements: rules must point to an array of rules with length rules_count.
rules_count must be >= 0.

Each rule’s fields must respect: device_class 0–255 or -1; vendor_id 0–65535 or -1; product_id 0–65535 or -1; device_version_bcd 0–65535 or -1; allow is an integer where 0 means deny and non-zero means allow.
Caller must check the integer return code before using the rules elsewhere.

functions.name: usbredirfilter_print
functions.signature: void usbredirfilter_print(const struct usbredirfilter_rule *rules, int rules_count, FILE *out);
functions.description: Prints the provided rules to the FILE stream out in a human-readable format. Intended for diagnostics or debugging; does not modify the rules.
requirements: rules must point to an array of rules with length rules_count.
rules_count must be >= 0.
out must be a valid, writable FILE* stream opened by the caller.
Caller should ensure thread-safe use of FILE* as appropriate for their environment.

functions.name: usbredirfilter_free
functions.signature: void usbredirfilter_free(void *ptr);
functions.description: Frees memory that was allocated by this library and returned to the caller (e.g., the rules array from usbredirfilter_string_to_rules or the string from usbredirfilter_rules_to_string). Use this instead of free for such allocations.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer previously returned by this library (e.g., from usbredirfilter_string_to_rules or usbredirfilter_rules_to_string).
Only pass pointers that this library allocated; do not use for arbitrary allocations from other allocators.
It is unspecified whether NULL is accepted; prefer passing a valid library-allocated pointer.

functions.name: usbredirparser_create
functions.signature: struct usbredirparser *usbredirparser_create(void);
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new usbredirparser instance. After creation, the caller must set priv and any needed callbacks on the returned struct, then call usbredirparser_init() before using the parser to read/write or send packets.
requirements: Must be followed by setting parser->priv and required callback function pointers before initialization.
Must call usbredirparser_init() before calling any other operational functions (e.g., do_read/do_write/send_*).
Returned pointer must be destroyed with usbredirparser_destroy() when no longer needed.

functions.name: usbredirparser_caps_set_cap
functions.signature: void usbredirparser_caps_set_cap(uint32_t *caps, int cap);
functions.description: Helper to set a capability bit in the capability array intended for usbredirparser_init().
requirements: caps must point to a capability array large enough for all capabilities (typically USB_REDIR_CAPS_SIZE elements).
cap must refer to a valid capability index as defined by the protocol.
Must be called before usbredirparser_init() when preparing the caps array.

functions.name: usbredirparser_init
functions.signature: void usbredirparser_init(struct usbredirparser *parser, const char *version, uint32_t *caps, int caps_len, int flags);
functions.description: Initializes the parser. Queues an initial hello packet with the provided version and capabilities and configures behavior based on flags (e.g., usbredirparser_fl_usb_host, usbredirparser_fl_write_cb_owns_buffer, usbredirparser_fl_no_hello).
requirements: parser must be a valid object created by usbredirparser_create().
Caller should have set parser->priv and required callbacks (read_func, write_func, log_func, and any packet callbacks to be used) before calling.
version should point to a valid version string expected by the peer.
caps must reference a capability array of length caps_len prepared by the caller (e.g., with usbredirparser_caps_set_cap); caps_len must match the array size.

If usbredirparser_fl_write_cb_owns_buffer is set, the write callback takes ownership of write buffers and must either accept the entire buffer (return count), report would-block (0), or error (-1); partial writes are not allowed and will trigger abort().

If usbredirparser_fl_no_hello is set, the usual initial hello exchange behavior may be suppressed; peer capability functions that depend on hello must not be called until the protocol state is appropriate.

functions.name: usbredirparser_destroy
functions.signature: void usbredirparser_destroy(struct usbredirparser *parser);
functions.description: Destroys a usbredirparser instance and releases its resources.
requirements: parser must have been created by usbredirparser_create().
Must not be used after destruction.
Should be called once per created parser.

functions.name: usbredirparser_have_cap
functions.signature: int usbredirparser_have_cap(struct usbredirparser *parser, int cap);
functions.description: Checks whether the local side (this parser) has a given capability, based on the capabilities provided at initialization.
requirements: parser must have been initialized via usbredirparser_init().
cap must be a valid capability index.

functions.name: usbredirparser_have_peer_caps
functions.signature: int usbredirparser_have_peer_caps(struct usbredirparser *parser);
functions.description: Returns nonzero if capabilities have been received from the peer (i.e., after the hello exchange), otherwise zero.
requirements: parser must be initialized.
Only returns true after the peer’s hello/capabilities have been received (typically after usbredirparser_do_read processes the peer’s hello).

functions.name: usbredirparser_peer_has_cap
functions.signature: int usbredirparser_peer_has_cap(struct usbredirparser *parser, int cap);
functions.description: Checks whether the peer has a specific capability. Intended for use after the hello exchange has completed.
requirements: parser must be initialized.
Should not be used before the hello_func callback has been called (i.e., before peer capabilities are known).
cap must be a valid capability index.

functions.name: usbredirparser_do_read
functions.signature: int usbredirparser_do_read(struct usbredirparser *parser);
functions.description: Parses incoming data by invoking the read callback to pull bytes from the transport, decoding packets, and dispatching the appropriate callbacks. On I/O or parse errors it resynchronizes as documented.
requirements: parser must be initialized and have a valid read_func set.
Caller should invoke whenever input data may be available.

Return values: 0 or positive on success/progress; usbredirparser_read_io_error (-1) for I/O errors; usbredirparser_read_parse_error (-2) for parse errors (parser skips to next packet based on length field).
On I/O error, the function continues where it left off on the next call; on parse error it skips to the next packet boundary.

functions.name: usbredirparser_has_data_to_write
functions.signature: int usbredirparser_has_data_to_write(struct usbredirparser *parser);
functions.description: Returns the number of usbredir packets queued for writing to the peer.
requirements: parser must be initialized.
A positive return value indicates data is pending; caller should then call usbredirparser_do_write().

functions.name: usbredirparser_get_bufferered_output_size
functions.signature: uint64_t usbredirparser_get_bufferered_output_size(struct usbredirparser *parser_pub);
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes currently queued to be written. Can be used by control logic to decide whether to drop pending data.
requirements: parser_pub must be initialized.
Interprets the internal output buffer state; no side effects.

functions.name: usbredirparser_do_write
functions.signature: int usbredirparser_do_write(struct usbredirparser *parser);
functions.description: Attempts to write queued packets to the peer using the write callback. Returns 0 on success or usbredirparser_write_io_error (-1) on write error; queued data will be retried on subsequent calls until it succeeds.
requirements: parser must be initialized and have a valid write_func set.
Should be called when usbredirparser_has_data_to_write() > 0.
If usbredirparser_fl_write_cb_owns_buffer was set at init, the write callback owns buffers and must accept the entire buffer or return would-block (0) or error (-1); partial writes are not permitted.

functions.name: usbredirparser_free_write_buffer
functions.signature: void usbredirparser_free_write_buffer(struct usbredirparser *parser, uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Releases a write buffer previously handed to the write callback when the parser was initialized with usbredirparser_fl_write_cb_owns_buffer.
requirements: Must only be called by the write callback (or code managing it) when usbredirparser_fl_write_cb_owns_buffer was specified at initialization.
data must be a buffer pointer previously provided by the parser to the write callback; do not pass arbitrary or user-allocated buffers.
parser must be valid (initialized or at least not destroyed).

functions.name: usbredirparser_free_packet_data
functions.signature: void usbredirparser_free_packet_data(struct usbredirparser *parser, uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Frees a data buffer received via a data packet callback (control, bulk, iso, interrupt, or buffered bulk). Ownership of such buffers is transferred to the callback, which must free them via this function when done.
requirements: Must only be called for buffers received through the data packet callbacks where ownership was explicitly transferred.
data must be the exact pointer received from the callback; do not free unrelated memory.
parser must be valid (not destroyed).

functions.name: usbredirparser_send_device_connect
functions.signature: void usbredirparser_send_device_connect(struct usbredirparser *parser, struct usb_redir_device_connect_header *device_connect);
functions.description: Queues a device-connect control packet for sending to the peer.
requirements: parser must be initialized.
Should not be used before the hello_func callback has been called (relies on usb_redir_cap_connect_device_version capability).
Packet is only queued; it will be transmitted when usbredirparser_do_write() is called.
If insufficient memory is available, the packet will be dropped and an error will be logged.

functions.name: usbredirparser_send_device_disconnect
functions.signature: void usbredirparser_send_device_disconnect(struct usbredirparser *parser);
functions.description: Queues a device-disconnect control packet to inform the peer the device is being disconnected.
requirements: parser must be initialized.
Actual transmission occurs via usbredirparser_do_write().
On low-memory conditions, the packet may be dropped and an error logged.

functions.name: usbredirparser_send_reset
functions.signature: void usbredirparser_send_reset(struct usbredirparser *parser);
functions.description: Queues a device reset control packet for sending to the peer.
requirements: parser must be initialized.
Packet is sent only when usbredirparser_do_write() is called.
On insufficient memory, the packet may be dropped with an error log.

functions.name: usbredirparser_send_interface_info
functions.signature: void usbredirparser_send_interface_info(struct usbredirparser *parser, struct usb_redir_interface_info_header *interface_info);
functions.description: Queues an interface_info control packet describing interface configuration details.
requirements: parser must be initialized.
Call usbredirparser_do_write() to transmit.
Low-memory conditions may cause the packet to be dropped with an error log.

functions.name: usbredirparser_send_ep_info
functions.signature: void usbredirparser_send_ep_info(struct usbredirparser *parser, struct usb_redir_ep_info_header *ep_info);
functions.description: Queues an endpoint information control packet.
requirements: parser must be initialized.
Transmission requires usbredirparser_do_write().
Packet may be dropped on out-of-memory and logged as an error.

functions.name: usbredirparser_send_set_configuration
functions.signature: void usbredirparser_send_set_configuration(struct usbredirparser *parser, uint64_t id, struct usb_redir_set_configuration_header *set_configuration);
functions.description: Queues a set_configuration control packet referencing a specific request id.
requirements: parser must be initialized.
id should be set per protocol expectations for matching responses.

functions.signature: void usbredirparser_send_get_configuration(struct usbredirparser *parser, uint64_t id);
functions.description: Queues a get_configuration request control packet with the given id.
requirements: parser must be initialized.
id must be set according to the protocol for correlating replies.

functions.name: usbredirhost_open
functions.signature:
struct usbredirhost *usbredirhost_open(
    libusb_context *usb_ctx,
    libusb_device_handle *usb_dev_handle,
    usbredirparser_log log_func,
    usbredirparser_read  read_guest_data_func,
    usbredirparser_write write_guest_data_func,
    void *func_priv, const char *version, int verbose, int flags);
functions.description: Create and initialize a usbredirhost instance (including an embedded usbredirparser) and send the initial usb_redir_hello to the guest. If usb_dev_handle is non-NULL, the host will immediately attempt to redirect that device via usbredirhost_set_device; on failure it destroys the new host and returns NULL. log_func is used for logging; read_guest_data_func/write_guest_data_func are transport I/O callbacks to read/write data to the usb-guest. Callers must ensure libusb_handle_events is serviced for the libusb_context from the provided libusb_device_handle when there are pending libusb pollfds. Callbacks (log and write) may be invoked before the function returns. Partially multi-thread safe (see docs/multi-thread.md).
requirements: usb_ctx must be a valid libusb_context suitable for any provided usb_dev_handle (unknown if NULL is allowed; follow library expectations).
If usb_dev_handle is not NULL, ownership is transferred to the usbredirhost; it may be closed on failure during initialization.
log_func must be a valid callback compatible with usbredirparser_log and callable during this function.
read_guest_data_func and write_guest_data_func must be valid callbacks; they may be called before this function returns.
version must be a valid NUL-terminated string describing the user of the library (semantics not otherwise specified).
verbose is an integer verbosity level (exact range not specified).
flags may include usbredirhost_fl_write_cb_owns_buffer to indicate write callback owns buffer; otherwise 0. Follow usbredirparser/host docs for semantics.
The embedding application must ensure libusb_handle_events is called when libusb_get_pollfds indicates pending events for the used libusb_context.

functions.name: usbredirhost_open_full
functions.signature:
struct usbredirhost *usbredirhost_open_full(
    libusb_context *usb_ctx,
    libusb_device_handle *usb_dev_handle,
    usbredirparser_log log_func,
    usbredirparser_read  read_guest_data_func,
    usbredirparser_write write_guest_data_func,
    usbredirhost_flush_writes flush_writes_func,
    usbredirparser_alloc_lock alloc_lock_func,
    usbredirparser_lock lock_func,
    usbredirparser_unlock unlock_func,
    usbredirparser_free_lock free_lock_func,
    void *func_priv, const char *version, int verbose, int flags);
functions.description: Create a usbredirhost with extended control over write flushing and locking (see docs/multi-thread.md). Besides the standard log/read/write callbacks, callers provide flush_writes and parser locking callbacks to integrate with their threading model. If usb_dev_handle is provided, the function attempts to set the device immediately (taking ownership); on failure the instance is destroyed and NULL returned. Callbacks may be invoked before this function returns. The application remains responsible for driving libusb_handle_events for the underlying libusb_context.
requirements: usb_ctx must reference a valid libusb_context compatible with any provided usb_dev_handle.
If usb_dev_handle is not NULL, ownership is transferred; it may be closed on failure.
log_func, read_guest_data_func, write_guest_data_func must be valid function pointers and callable during initialization.
flush_writes_func (if provided by API contract; header requires a pointer) must be a valid callback that flushes any buffered transport writes when requested.
alloc_lock_func, lock_func, unlock_func, free_lock_func must be valid callbacks implementing a lock compatible with usbredirparser expectations (details in docs/multi-thread.md).
version must be a valid NUL-terminated string; verbose an integer; flags may include usbredirhost_fl_write_cb_owns_buffer.
The embedding application must ensure libusb_handle_events is called when libusb reports pending events.

functions.name: usbredirhost_close
functions.signature: void usbredirhost_close(struct usbredirhost *host);
functions.description: Destroy the usbredirhost instance. If a USB device is currently redirected, this first performs a disconnect by calling usbredirhost_set_device(host, NULL) (see that function’s notes), then frees all resources.
requirements: host must be a valid usbredirhost pointer previously returned by usbredirhost_open/_full and not already closed.
After return, the host pointer is invalid and must not be used.
Caller must be prepared that, during the internal disconnect, libusb_handle_events may be called (see usbredirhost_set_device notes) which can invoke libusb completion callbacks in the application.

functions.name: usbredirhost_set_device
functions.signature:
int usbredirhost_set_device(struct usbredirhost *host,
                            libusb_device_handle *usb_dev_handle);
functions.description: Attach or detach a libusb device to be redirected. When passed a valid libusb_device_handle, the host sends initial device information (interface_info, ep_info, device_connect) to the guest and makes the device available to it. Passing NULL disconnects any currently redirected device and returns it to the local OS. Ownership semantics: when a non-NULL handle is passed in, usbredirhost takes ownership; the handle is closed on failure and any previously redirected device is disconnected and closed. During disconnect, the function may call libusb_handle_events to reap canceled URBs, which can fire completion callbacks in the application.
requirements: host must be a valid usbredirhost.
If usb_dev_handle is non-NULL, it must be an open libusb_device_handle; ownership is transferred to the usbredirhost upon call.
On failure when attaching, the passed usb_dev_handle may be closed by the function; caller must not use it afterwards.
If a device is already redirected on host, calling with a new non-NULL handle will disconnect and close the old device.

When disconnecting (passing NULL), the function may call libusb_handle_events to reap canceled transfers; the application must be prepared for its libusb transfer completion callbacks to be invoked during this call.
Return value is a usbredirproto status code (e.g., usb_redir_success); caller must check and handle non-success codes.

functions.name: usbredirhost_set_buffered_output_size_cb
functions.signature:
void usbredirhost_set_buffered_output_size_cb(struct usbredirhost *host,
    usbredirhost_buffered_output_size buffered_output_size_func);
functions.description: Register a callback that reports the application’s pending write buffer size in bytes. usbredirhost uses this information to set thresholds (based on USB device characteristics) to drop isochronous packets when the application’s buffer grows too much, while still trying to send full frames when possible.
requirements: host must be a valid usbredirhost.
buffered_output_size_func must be a valid function pointer returning the current number of pending output bytes in the application.
The callback may be called by usbredirhost at arbitrary times; it should be fast and safe w.r.t. the application’s threading model (details unspecified).

functions.name: usbredirhost_read_guest_data
functions.signature: int usbredirhost_read_guest_data(struct usbredirhost *host);
functions.description: Process incoming data available from the usb-guest by reading from the application-provided transport and parsing packets. Returns 0 on success; on error, returns one of the negative codes: usbredirhost_read_io_error, usbredirhost_read_parse_error, usbredirhost_read_device_rejected, or usbredirhost_read_device_lost. On IO error the next call continues where it left off; on parse error it skips to the next packet; on device_rejected the caller is expected to disconnect via usbredirhost_set_device(host, NULL); on device_lost the host has already performed the equivalent device disconnect.
requirements: host must be a valid usbredirhost with functional read_guest_data_func set at open time.
Call this when there is data ready for the usbredirhost to read from the usb-guest transport.
Caller must check the return value and handle negative codes as documented: on usbredirhost_read_device_rejected, call usbredirhost_set_device(host, NULL).
No additional assumptions about blocking behavior are documented; integrate with your transport’s readiness model.

functions.name: usbredirhost_has_data_to_write
functions.signature: int usbredirhost_has_data_to_write(struct usbredirhost *host);
functions.description: Return the number of usbredir packets currently queued for writing to the usb-guest. Use this to decide whether to call usbredirhost_write_guest_data.
requirements: host must be a valid usbredirhost.
Caller should interpret a return value > 0 as pending data that should be flushed via usbredirhost_write_guest_data.

functions.name: usbredirhost_write_guest_data
functions.signature: int usbredirhost_write_guest_data(struct usbredirhost *host);
functions.description: Write queued usbredir packets to the usb-guest using the application’s write callback. Returns 0 on success, or usbredirhost_write_io_error (-1) if a write error occurred. If a write error occurs, the function retains queued data and will retry on subsequent calls until it succeeds.
requirements: host must be a valid usbredirhost.
Should be called when usbredirhost_has_data_to_write(host) returns > 0.
Caller must handle a return value of -1 as a transient write error and call again to retry; the function will continue retrying queued data until success.
The write callback provided at open time must remain valid for the lifetime of the host.

functions.name: usbredirhost_free_write_buffer
functions.signature: void usbredirhost_free_write_buffer(struct usbredirhost *host, uint8_t *data);
functions.description: Free a data buffer previously passed to the application’s write_guest_data_func when the usbredirhost_fl_write_cb_owns_buffer flag was used at open time. This hands buffer lifetime management back to usbredirhost when the write callback owns the buffer.
requirements: host must be a valid usbredirhost.
Only call this if usbredirhost was opened with the usbredirhost_fl_write_cb_owns_buffer flag.
data must be the same buffer pointer previously provided to the write_guest_data_func by usbredirhost and must not be freed by the caller by other means.

    const struct usbredirfilter_rule **rules_ret, int *rules_count_ret);
functions.description: Retrieve the filter rules provided by the usbredir-guest, if any. On return, *rules_ret points to the guest’s rule array and *rules_count_ret holds its length; if no filter exists, *rules_ret is set to NULL and *rules_count_ret to 0.

The returned rule pointer is owned by usbredirhost; the caller must not modify or free it.

functions.name: usbredirhost_check_device_filter
functions.signature:
int usbredirhost_check_device_filter(const struct usbredirfilter_rule *rules,
    int rules_count, libusb_device *dev, int flags);
functions.description: Fetch the device and configuration descriptors from the given libusb_device and evaluate them against the provided usbredir filter rules by calling usbredirfilter_check. flags are forwarded as-is to usbredirfilter_check. Returns -EIO or -ENOMEM if descriptor retrieval fails; otherwise returns whatever usbredirfilter_check returns.

rules_count must be >= 0.

flags are passed through to usbredirfilter_check; valid values are those accepted by that API (see its documentation).
Caller must handle return values: -EIO/-ENOMEM indicate descriptor read failures; other values are defined by usbredirfilter_check.

import random
import struct
import string

# Generator for "arbitrary bytes" consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# Target stubs:
# - usbredirfilter_check: Uses up to three strings to fill interface class/subclass/protocol arrays, and many
#   integers pulled via FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int). We provide a buffer that encodes a sequence of 32-bit ints
#   followed by several varied byte strings so the harness can slice values. Although the harness treats the
#   bytes opaquely, providing diverse lengths and byte ranges increases valid/interesting coverage while
#   remaining valid arbitrary bytes.
# - usbredirparser_init: Uses a version string and a few random caps indices. Provide a plausible ASCII
#   version prefix followed by random and non-ASCII bytes to exercise string handling while remaining valid.
# - usbredirparser_unserialize: Requires a buffer; we include multiple segments and lengths to vary inputs.
#
# Strategy:
# - Construct a header with many 32-bit unsigned integers to satisfy multiple FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) pulls.
# - Append multiple strings with different characteristics (ASCII, numeric-only, binary with NULs, repeated
#   patterns, high-entropy) separated by small random separators. The harness uses the entire buffer as a source
#   for each FUZZ_PARAM_STR independently, so ensuring overall diversity is sufficient.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

ASCII_VERSION_PREFIXES = [
    b"usbredir/1.0", b"usbredir/2.0", b"usbredir-fuzz", b"qemu-usbredir", b"spice-usbredir"
]


def _rand_u32(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Favor values that hit edge cases and typical ranges
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 255, 256, 1024, 4096, 65535, 65536, 2**31-1, 2**31, 2**32-1]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.getrandbits(32)
    return rng.choice(choices)


def _make_u32_block(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> bytes:
    return b"".join(struct.pack("<I", _rand_u32(rng)) for _ in range(count))


def _make_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " ._-:/,;"
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))
    return s.encode('ascii')


def _make_binary(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(length))


def _make_pattern(rng: random.Random, patterns) -> bytes:
    pat = rng.choice(patterns)
    reps = rng.randint(1, 64)
    return pat * reps


def _cap_bits_blob(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a capability-like area: sparse bits set in a fixed-size array (8 u32 = 256 caps)
    caps = [0] * 8
    set_count = rng.randint(0, 10)
    for _ in range(set_count):
        cap = rng.randint(0, 255)
        idx = cap // 32
        bit = cap % 32
        caps[idx] |= (1 << bit)
    return b"".join(struct.pack("<I", x) for x in caps)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # 1) Numeric header: many u32 values for FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int)
    # Ensure enough for both stubs (filter_check uses several; parser_init uses some; others may consume more).
    u32_count = rng.randint(32, 96)
    buf = bytearray()
    buf += _make_u32_block(rng, u32_count)

    # 2) Version-like string candidate (ASCII), with trailing NUL sometimes
    ver = bytearray()
    ver += rng.choice(ASCII_VERSION_PREFIXES)
    # Append dotted components and random ascii tail
    tail = _make_ascii(rng, 0, 20)
    if tail:
        ver += b"-" + tail
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        ver += b"\x00"
    # Prepend a small length to help consumers that might read size-prefixed slices
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        buf += struct.pack("<I", len(ver))
    buf += ver

    # 3) Interface class/subclass/proto bytes: include distinct strings with varied bytes
    # ASCII-only
    ifaceA = _make_ascii(rng, 1, 32)
    # Binary with NULs
    ifaceB = _make_binary(rng, 1, 32)
    # Patterned data to create repetition
    ifaceC = _make_pattern(rng, [b"\x00", b"\xff", b"ABC", b"\x01\x02", b"\xaa\x55"])[:32]

    # Optionally include small separators
    sep = bytes([rng.choice([0x00, 0x2c, 0x3b, 0xff])]) * rng.randint(0, 3)
    buf += sep + ifaceA + sep + ifaceB + sep + ifaceC

    # 4) Capability bitmap blob for parser_init caps
    buf += _cap_bits_blob(rng)

    # 5) Additional strings to feed other FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls with variety
    blobs = []
    blobs.append(_make_ascii(rng, 0, 64))
    blobs.append(_make_binary(rng, 0, 128))
    blobs.append(_make_pattern(rng, [b"ver", b"cap", b"usb", b"redir"]))
    blobs.append(_make_binary(rng, 0, 256))
    rng.shuffle(blobs)
    for b in blobs:
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            buf += struct.pack("<I", len(b))
        buf += b

    # 6) Ensure total size constraint
    if len(buf) > 4096:
        buf = buf[:4096]

    return bytes(buf)

from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces a valid textual filter description for usbredirfilter rules
# that can be fed to a harness which will turn it into struct usbredirfilter_rule[]
# and later print it via usbredirfilter_print into a fuzz-provided file. Although the
# target stub only opens a filename and writes to it, many fuzzing setups reuse the
# same initial buffer as input for other stubs (e.g., rules parser). Therefore we
# craft a filter string covering various value ranges and separators, remaining valid.
#
# Rule format (consumed by usbredirfilter_string_to_rules):
#   "<class>,<vendor>,<product>,<version>,<allow>" with token separators and rule
#   separators (like strtok). Fields can be -1 for wildcard; otherwise numeric ranges:
#   class 0..255; vendor/product/version 0..65535; allow 0/1.
#
# We emit a buffer containing:
#  - Custom token/rule separators on the first line as a hint to the harness
#    (e.g., token seps " ,;:" and rule seps "\n;|")
#  - Then a rules string using a mix of separators from those sets
#  - We keep bytes <= 0x7f and include newlines; total <= 4096 bytes.

TOKEN_SEPS_DEFAULT = ", :\t"  # typical token separators set
RULE_SEPS_DEFAULT = "\n;|"     # typical rule separators set


def _rand_bool(rng: random.Random) -> bool:
    return rng.randint(0, 1) == 1


def _pick(rng: random.Random, arr: List):
    return arr[rng.randrange(len(arr))]


def _gen_numeric(rng: random.Random, bits: int) -> int:
    # Biased selection to hit edges and typical values
    if bits == 8:
        choices = [0, 1, 3, 0x03, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0a, 0x0b, 0x0e, 0xef, 0xff]
        # keep within 0..255
        return min(255, max(0, _pick(rng, choices))) if _rand_bool(rng) else rng.randint(0, 255)
    elif bits == 16:
        choices = [0, 1, 0x0100, 0x0200, 0x1234, 0x046d, 0x05ac, 0x18d1, 0xffff]
        return min(65535, max(0, _pick(rng, choices))) if _rand_bool(rng) else rng.randint(0, 65535)
    else:
        return 0


def _gen_field(rng: random.Random, bits: int) -> str:
    # Sometimes wildcard -1, otherwise number
    if _rand_bool(rng):
        return "-1"
    return str(_gen_numeric(rng, bits))


def _gen_allow(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return "1" if _rand_bool(rng) else "0"


def _compose_rule(rng: random.Random, token_seps: str) -> str:
    # Construct with random token separators chosen between fields
    tokens = [
        _gen_field(rng, 8),      # class
        _gen_numeric(rng, 8) if _rand_bool(rng) and _rand_bool(rng) else _gen_field(rng, 16),  # sometimes small vendor
        _gen_field(rng, 16),     # product
        _gen_field(rng, 16),     # version bcd
        _gen_allow(rng),         # allow
    ]
    # Turn second element to string (may be int)
    tokens = [str(t) for t in tokens]
    # Join with random separators from token_seps
    parts = []
    for i, t in enumerate(tokens):
        parts.append(t)
        if i != len(tokens) - 1:
            parts.append(_pick(rng, list(token_seps)))
    return "".join(parts)


def _gen_rules_string(rng: random.Random, token_seps: str, rule_seps: str, count: int) -> str:
    rules = []
    for _ in range(count):
        rules.append(_compose_rule(rng, token_seps))
    # Join with a mixture of rule separators
    out = []
    for i, r in enumerate(rules):
        out.append(r)
        if i != len(rules) - 1:
            out.append(_pick(rng, list(rule_seps)))
    return "".join(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Randomize separator sets slightly while keeping them reasonable ASCII
    token_seps_pool = [",", " ", ":", "\t", "\r"]
    rule_seps_pool = ["\n", ";", "|", "\r\n"]

    # Build token/rule separator strings (distinct characters; length 2..4)
    token_seps = "".join(rng.sample(token_seps_pool, rng.randint(2, 4)))
    rule_seps = "".join(rng.sample(["\n", ";", "|"], rng.randint(2, 3)))

    # Number of rules: 5..40, but cap final size <= 4096
    rule_count = rng.randint(8, 24)

    rules_str = _gen_rules_string(rng, token_seps, rule_seps, rule_count)

    # Some harnesses accept a header line describing separators; include as comment-like
    # prefix lines the consumer can ignore if not used. Keep purely ASCII.
    header_lines = [
        f"# token_seps={token_seps}",
        f"# rule_seps={rule_seps}",
    ]

    blob = "\n".join(header_lines) + "\n" + rules_str + "\n"

    # Ensure size <= 4096; if exceeded, trim trailing rules safely at a rule boundary
    b = blob.encode("ascii", errors="ignore")
    if len(b) > 4096:
        # Trim at last rule separator within limit
        cut = 4096
        sub = b[:cut]
        last_sep = max(sub.rfind(ord("\n").to_bytes(1, 'little')), sub.rfind(b";"), sub.rfind(b"|"))
        if last_sep == -1:
            b = sub
        else:
            b = sub[: last_sep + 1]
    return b

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: Generate initial buffers for FUZZ_PARAM_STR used as version strings in:
# - usbredirparser_init (version string)
# - usbredirhost_open (version string)
# Data type: NUL-terminated version/identification string; consumers should handle arbitrary bytes.
# Strategy: Return a bytes blob that the harness will slice to feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# We construct a corpus of plausible version strings concatenated with separators so
# the fuzzer can extract interesting substrings. Include:
# - Semantic versions with/without prerelease/build metadata
# - Long strings near 64 bytes (hello header has 64-char version field)
# - Non-ASCII UTF-8, control chars, and embedded NUL handling (end at first NUL)
# - Edge cases: empty, single char, very long, repeated patterns
# Keep total under 4096 bytes.

SEP = b"\n\0\n"  # Provide explicit NULs; consumers read C-strings up to first NUL.

PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " .-_+/@:()[]{}#"


def _rand_semver(r: random.Random) -> str:
    major = r.randint(0, 50)
    minor = r.randint(0, 50)
    patch = r.randint(0, 200)
    base = f"{major}.{minor}.{patch}"
    parts: List[str] = [base]
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        # pre-release
        label = r.choice(["alpha", "beta", "rc", "dev"])
        n = r.randint(0, 9)
        parts.append(f"-{label}.{n}")
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        # build metadata
        meta_segs = [
            ''.join(r.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)))
            for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3))
        ]
        parts.append("+" + ".".join(meta_segs))
    return "".join(parts)


def _rand_printable(r: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(r.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n))


def _utf8_mix(r: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix ASCII and multibyte UTF-8 (e.g., emoji, CJK), plus some controls except NUL
    blocks: List[bytes] = []
    while sum(len(b) for b in blocks) < target_len:
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.6:
            blocks.append(_rand_printable(r, r.randint(1, 8)).encode('ascii'))
        elif choice < 0.8:
            # common unicode ranges
            cp = r.choice([
                0x00A9, 0x00AE, 0x03B1, 0x03C0, 0x20AC, 0x2603, 0x2713,
                0x4E2D, 0x56FD, 0x65E5, 0x672C, 0xD83D, 0xDE80
            ])
            try:
                blocks.append(chr(cp).encode('utf-8'))
            except Exception:
                pass
        else:
            # control chars excluding NUL
            ctrl = r.choice([0x01, 0x02, 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0D, 0x1B])
            blocks.append(bytes([ctrl]))
    out = b''.join(blocks)
    return out[:target_len]


def _aligned64_variants() -> List[bytes]:
    # Exactly 64 and near-64 bytes to exercise fixed-size hello version[64]
    base = b"usbredir/1.0 minimal"
    fill = b"X" * (64 - len(base)) if len(base) < 64 else b""
    exact64 = (base + fill)[:64]
    near_under = b"Y" * 63
    near_over = (b"Z" * 70)
    return [exact64, near_under, near_over]


def _well_known() -> List[bytes]:
    return [
        b"usbredir-0.13.0",
        b"QEMU-usbredir/4.2",
        b"Spice-USB-Redirection/0.12.10",
        b"libusbredirhost/2.0",
        b"1.0",
        b"",  # empty
        b"v",
        b"0",
        b"unknown",
    ]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    pieces: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Start with a semver-like main string
    pieces.append(_rand_semver(r).encode('ascii'))

    # 2) Add known variants
    pieces.extend(_well_known())

    # 3) Include exactly/near 64-byte strings
    pieces.extend(_aligned64_variants())

    # 4) A long printable banner including tokens often seen in version strings
    banner = (
        f"usbredirhost { _rand_semver(r) } ({_rand_printable(r, r.randint(4,12))}) "
        f"build:{r.randint(1000,999999)} commit:{_rand_printable(r,7)}"
    ).encode('ascii')
    pieces.append(banner)

    # 5) UTF-8 rich variant with length 64-192 bytes
    utf_len = r.randint(64, 192)
    pieces.append(_utf8_mix(r, utf_len))

    # 6) Add a case with embedded NUL mid-string then more data after; C-string will stop at first NUL
    pre = _rand_printable(r, r.randint(3, 12)).encode('ascii')
    post = _rand_printable(r, r.randint(3, 12)).encode('ascii')
    pieces.append(pre + b"\0" + post)

    # 7) Repeated pattern and whitespace-only
    patt = (b"ver:" + _rand_semver(r).encode('ascii') + b" ") * r.randint(2, 6)
    pieces.append(patt)
    pieces.append(b" \t \r\n")

    # 8) Random printable with length around 64
    pieces.append(_rand_printable(r, r.randint(50, 80)).encode('ascii'))

    # 9) Very long but bounded string to test truncation/handling (<= 1024)
    long_part = _rand_printable(r, r.randint(256, 512)).encode('ascii')
    pieces.append(long_part)

    # Interleave separators containing NUL to allow multiple distinct C-strings
    out = b""
    for i, p in enumerate(pieces):
        out += p
        # Insert separator except maybe after last
        if i != len(pieces) - 1:
            out += SEP

    # Ensure total size <= 4096
    return out[:4096]
